name: Steve Cohen
bio: Memphis-area Democratic congressman serving since 2007. Announced May 15, 2026 he would not seek reelection after redistricting dismantled TN-9, but left the door open if legal challenges succeed. cohenforcongress.com remains active and he cosponsored the Universal School Meals Program Act of 2026 (H.R. 8798) in May 2026.
status_line: Conditional retirement announced May 15, 2026 · Active if redistricting lawsuit succeeds

early_childhood_ed.summary: Cohen has a long record of securing federal funding for Head Start, Early Head Start, and pre-K programs in the Memphis area. In June 2026, he took action to protect vulnerable children enrolled in the state's Children's Special Services program. In July 2026, a Nashville court extended an order blocking immigration-status reporting requirements for sick and disabled children. On July 9, 2026, Cohen published an op-ed in The Commercial Appeal formally endorsing London Lamar for Congress, in which he reflected on his legacy of securing federal investments for Memphis including 'education initiatives and economic development throughout our community.' Multiple sources published July 7–13 confirm Cohen is now fully retired from the race, referring to him as 'the outgoing representative.' No new early childhood education statements were found in the July 7–13, 2026 window.
early_childhood_ed.details: Cohen's July 9 endorsement op-ed mentioned his broader legacy of federal investment in Memphis communities, including education initiatives, but contained no specific new statements on early childhood education, Head Start, or pre-K. Coverage in WREG (July 7), Tennessee Lookout (July 8), DNYUZ (July 8), and other outlets confirmed he is the 'outgoing' congressman and has decisively stepped aside — ending any conditionality in his May retirement announcement. No lawsuit update restoring the former majority-Black TN-9 map was found in this window.

child_hunger.summary: Cohen cosponsored H.R. 8798 (Universal School Meals Program Act of 2026, May 13, 2026), which would provide free meals to every student nationwide and reverse SNAP cuts enacted by the One Big Beautiful Bill. As of July 7–13, 2026, new reporting confirmed that approximately 100,000 Tennesseans have now lost SNAP food benefits under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, with total SNAP recipients in Tennessee falling from 696,000 in July 2025 to 597,890 in May 2026. Cohen made no new public statements on child hunger during the July 7–13 window; his July 9 op-ed focused on endorsing London Lamar and reflecting on his congressional legacy.
child_hunger.details: A July 10 Tennessee Lookout investigation (republished July 10 in the Daily Gazette) documented the scale of SNAP loss in Tennessee — approximately one in seven recipients since July 2025. The article noted that children aging out of foster care and individuals experiencing homelessness are among those now subject to new work requirements under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Cohen's own earlier cosponsorship of the Universal School Meals Program Act remains the most recent specific legislative action on child hunger. No new Cohen statements on child hunger were found in the July 7–13, 2026 window.

parental_support.summary: Cohen reintroduced the Latonya Reeves Freedom Act in June 2026 with 48 bipartisan cosponsors, a disability rights bill that would codify the right to home- and community-based long-term care services — directly supporting families of children with complex medical needs. On July 9, 2026, Cohen published an endorsement op-ed in The Commercial Appeal in which he described his congressional legacy as including 'services for veterans through organizations such as Alpha Omega, education initiatives and economic development throughout our community.' Multiple sources published July 7–13 confirm Cohen has stepped aside fully. No new parental support policy statements were found in the July 7–13, 2026 window.
